description: Data breach and cyber incident reporting obligations in South Africa, Nigeria, Kenya, Egypt, Ghana, Morocco, Rwanda, Uganda, Tanzania, Mauritius and Botswana: which regulators and people must be notified, the legal deadline (such as 72 hours) and the computed due time from discovery. Covers POPIA and FSCA/PA rules in South Africa, NDPA and ngCERT in Nigeria, and Kenya's Data Protection Act. Triage guidance, not legal advice. Price: $0.01 USDC per call (x402, Base mainnet).

aware_at.description: When you discovered the compromise (ISO 8601; no offset = UTC+2)

classified_at.description: Financial institutions: when the incident was classified as material (ISO 8601)

country.description: Country code: ZA (default), NG, KE, EG, GH, MA, RW, UG, TZ, MU or BW

critical_infrastructure.description: Outside South Africa: are you a designated critical / vital infrastructure operator? Omit if unknown

jse_listed.description: Is the organisation listed on the JSE? Default false

material.description: Financial institutions: has the incident been classified as material? Omit if not yet assessed

personal_info.description: Was personal information accessed or acquired by an unauthorised person? Omit if unknown

role.description: responsible_party (default) or operator (you process the data for someone else)

sector.description: South Africa only. Organisation type: general (any private business), bank, mutual_bank, insurer, financial_other (other FSCA-regulated institutions covered by Joint Standard 1 of 2023 or 2 of 2024, e.g. market infrastructures, certain FSPs, pension funds), public_body, ecsp (electronic communications service provider). Default general
